summaryZh: 文章通过伊利诺伊州农民Steve Pittstick 52年适应农业技术变迁的经历，以及爱荷华州立大学推广专家Doug Houser的观察，论述了人工智能和先进农机正在加速改变农业，农民应尽早了解、试用并采纳AI技术，而非因犹豫而落后。文章强调AI投资回报清晰、采纳速度将快于自动驾驶等技术，并给出“先理解、再 trial、后扩展”的实践建议。
featuredReason: 文章以一线农民和推广专家的真实视角，清晰论证了AI在农业中加速落地的趋势，并给出“先理解、再试用、后扩展”的可操作路径，对智慧畜牧从业者思考AI采纳节奏与数据价值具有直接借鉴意义。

Farming’s ‘Wild West’ requires early tech adoption over hesitation

Farmer Iron: Steve Pittstick has spent 52 years adapting to new farm technology — and believes artificial intelligence will separate successful farmers from those left behind.

Andy Castillo,Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery,Farm ProgressOctober 17, 2026

schedule3 Min Read

Modern farm technology is on display at the 2026 Farm Progress Show. Artificial intelligence and advanced machinery are rapidly transforming agriculture and challenging farmers to adopt them or risk falling behind. Andy Castillo

Illinois farmer Steve Pittstick can remember blasting an AM radio on the fender of his father’s tractor while rumbling across guess rows.

“Mom could hear me in the dooryard, but I couldn’t hear it sitting on the tractor,” Pittstick recalled while perusing the latest ag tech at this year’s Farm Progress Show in Boone, Iowa.

Farm technology has changed a lot since AM radios and open-air cabs of the last half-century. Today’s tractors boast more than 800 hp. Their interiors look like cars. Drones spray crops out in the field, and artificial intelligence is revolutionizing office work.

Pittstick, who is in his 52nd year farming, is embracing change — even if it’s disconcerting.

“We’re in the Wild West. I’m leery; I’m not all in. But I think we need to look at it. It’s going to be part of our life,” he said.

Evolving with technology is nothing new for Pittstick. He has been collecting yield data since 1996, and immediately recognized autosteer’s value in 2004.

Related:New Case IH Nutri-Tiller 1000 has 16 rows, planter integration

Recently, Pittstick joined 15 other farmers working with an AI developer that’s building a model capable of monitoring crop operations, documenting hybrid planting dates, collecting weather data and reporting on growth stages.

“It’s pretty cool stuff,” he said about the AI’s capability, which he thinks will solve the challenge of tracking data across operations. “My dad was an early adopter; my grandfather was an early adopter of technology. So naturally, I look for the next thing.”

Artificial intelligence

U.S. farmers can take a page from Pittstick’s playbook. Global industry is rapidly evolving as AI streamlines inefficiencies. Given its reliance on data, farming isn’t exempt from its reach.

Doug Houser, digital ag specialist at Iowa State University Extension, expects change will happen sooner rather than later. He has seen technology overhaul practices once thought unchangeable.

“I still remember climbing up in a combine, and I had a bag phone at that time. I had a farmer look at me and say, ‘Well, that’ll never replace my two-way radio. You wasted your money,’ ” Houser said.

Compared to other revolutionary technologies like autosteer, Houser expects AI’s adoption to happen much faster because its return on investment is clear. What does that mean for farmers?

“My recommendation for farmers is to understand the technology. Don’t get left out if there’s an option to get into a trial,” he said. With drones, “get some acres sprayed because you’re not going to believe in it until you have it on your acres. Then maybe take the next step.”

Related:Allis-Chalmers D21: Pioneering the modern tractor cab era

Tomorrow’s farmers won’t be replaced by AI, but by their neighbor who has embraced it.

Pittstick predicts AI systems will give adopters a leg up by completing practical tasks such as providing alerts for herbicide application windows based on weather, growth stage and product cutoff dates. With margins thinner than ever, every second counts.

“Don’t be afraid of it, embrace it. You don’t have to use it in your operation, but don’t keep it at arm’s length. Understand what it can or can’t do and prepare for it,” Pittstick said.

About the Author

Andy Castillo

Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery, Farm Progress

Andy Castillo started his career in journalism about a decade ago as a television news cameraperson and producer before transitioning to a regional newspaper covering western Massachusetts, where he wrote about local farming. Between military deployments with the Air Force and covering the news, he earned an MFA in creative nonfiction writing from Bay Path University, building on the English degree he earned from the University of Massachusetts Amherst. In his role at Farm Progress, Castillo covers agricultural technology, new machinery and the constantly evolving farm equipment marketplace.

Castillo splits his time between the open road and western Massachusetts with his wife, Brianna, a travel nurse who specializes in pediatric oncology, and their rescue pup, Rio. When not attending farm shows, Castillo enjoys playing music, snowboarding, writing, cooking and restoring their 1920 craftsman bungalow. You can find Castillo at farm machinery shows across the country.

translationZh:
伊利诺伊州农民Steve Pittstick还记得，当年他开着父亲的拖拉机在田间来回作业时，把一台AM收音机放在挡泥板上大声播放。

“妈妈在院子里都能听到，但我坐在拖拉机上却听不见。”Pittstick在今年于爱荷华州布恩举行的Farm Progress Show上浏览最新农业科技时回忆道。

自AM收音机和敞篷驾驶室以来的半个世纪，农业技术已经发生了巨大变化。如今的拖拉机功率超过800马力，内饰看起来像汽车。无人机在田间喷洒作物，人工智能正在革新办公室工作。

务农已进入第52个年头的Pittstick正在拥抱变化——即便这让人有些不安。

“我们正处在狂野西部。我很警惕，并没有全盘投入。但我认为我们需要关注它。它将成为我们生活的一部分。”他说。

对Pittstick来说，与技术共同演进并不新鲜。他自1996年以来一直在收集产量数据，并在2004年立刻认识到自动转向的价值。

近期，Pittstick与其他15位农民一起，与一家AI开发商合作，该开发商正在构建一个能够监测作物作业、记录杂交种种植日期、收集天气数据并报告生长阶段的模型。

“这东西相当酷。”他谈到AI的能力时说，他认为这将解决跨作业追踪数据的难题。“我父亲是早期采纳者，我祖父也是技术的早期采纳者。所以很自然，我会寻找下一个新事物。”

**人工智能**

美国农民可以借鉴Pittstick的经验。随着AI简化低效环节，全球产业正在迅速演变。鉴于农业对数据的依赖，它也无法置身于AI的影响之外。

爱荷华州立大学推广数字农业专家Doug Houser预计，变化会 sooner rather than later 发生。他见证过技术彻底改变曾被认为不可更改的做法。

“我还记得爬上联合收割机时，当时我带着一部袋装电话。一位农民看着我说：‘嗯，那永远取代不了我的双向无线电。你浪费钱了。’”Houser说。

与自动转向等其他革命性技术相比，Houser预计AI的采纳会快得多，因为其投资回报清晰。这对农民意味着什么？

“我对农民的建议是理解这项技术。如果有机会参与 trial，不要被落下。”他说。以无人机为例，“先让一些 acres 被喷洒，因为直到它在你自己的田里运行，你才会相信它。然后也许再迈出下一步。”

明天的农民不会被AI取代，而是会被拥抱AI的邻居取代。

Pittstick预测，AI系统将通过完成诸如根据天气、生长阶段和产品截止日期提供除草剂施用窗口警报等实用任务，让采纳者占据优势。在利润比以往更微薄的情况下，每一秒都很重要。

“不要害怕它，拥抱它。你不必在经营中用它，但不要把它拒之门外。了解它能做什么或不能做什么，并为此做好准备。”Pittstick说。
contentHtml: Farmer Iron: Steve Pittstick has spent 52 years adapting to new farm technology — and believes artificial intelligence will separate successful farmers from those left behind.
